description: How speech is INTERPRETED — from peripheral auditory analysis to discrete categories and words, and the core problems (invariance, segmentation) that make it hard.

sub_mechanisms.name: peripheral_auditory_analysis
sub_mechanisms.definition: The cochlea performs a running short-term frequency analysis (a bank of overlapping bandpass filters on a roughly log-frequency / ERB scale); the auditory nerve encodes the resulting time-frequency pattern (place + temporal code).
sub_mechanisms.why: The front end every higher process reads; it turns pressure-over-time into a tonotopic spectrogram-like representation — the agent's cochlea + A1 is exactly this stage.

sub_mechanisms.name: acoustic_cues
sub_mechanisms.definition: The specific properties of the signal that signal a phonetic contrast: VOT, formant frequencies + transitions, burst spectrum, spectral tilt, duration, amplitude envelope. A contrast is usually carried by MULTIPLE cues that trade off.
sub_mechanisms.why: Perception is the inverse of production — it must read these cues off the signal to recover place/manner/voicing.

sub_mechanisms.name: formant_transitions
sub_mechanisms.definition: The rapid movements of F2/F3 into and out of a consonant point back toward a virtual 'locus' frequency characteristic of the place of articulation.
sub_mechanisms.why: The dominant cue to consonant PLACE; a clear case where dynamic, context-dependent acoustics carry a category.

sub_mechanisms.name: categorical_perception
sub_mechanisms.definition: A continuous acoustic dimension (e.g. VOT, F2 onset) is perceived as discrete categories: a SHARP identification boundary, with discrimination that is good ACROSS the boundary but poor WITHIN a category.
sub_mechanisms.why: The signature finding of speech perception — the listener hears phonemes, not a continuum; it is what the agent's clustering/categorisation must reproduce.

sub_mechanisms.name: perceptual_magnet_effect
sub_mechanisms.definition: Within a native category, exemplars near the prototype are perceptually 'pulled' toward it, warping the acoustic space so within-category differences shrink near the centre (Kuhl).
sub_mechanisms.why: Explains how learned categories reshape the perceptual metric itself — native categories are not just labels but distortions of the space.

sub_mechanisms.name: lack_of_invariance
sub_mechanisms.definition: There is NO single invariant acoustic pattern for a phoneme: its realisation varies with coarticulatory context, speaker (vocal-tract length, pitch), and speaking rate. The same sound has many spectra; different sounds can share one.
sub_mechanisms.why: THE central problem of speech perception; any recogniser that assumes a fixed template per phoneme fails on it.

sub_mechanisms.name: speaker_normalization
sub_mechanisms.definition: Factoring out talker-specific differences — scaling for vocal-tract length (formant frequencies shift), pitch range, and rate — to recover the speaker-independent category (e.g. by formant ratios or extrinsic normalisation).
sub_mechanisms.why: One half of the answer to lack-of-invariance; without it a child's and an adult's /i/ look like different vowels.

sub_mechanisms.name: segmentation
sub_mechanisms.definition: The acoustic signal is continuous with no reliable silences at word or phoneme boundaries; the listener must parse the stream using prosody, allophonic cues, and lexical knowledge.
sub_mechanisms.why: You cannot recognise words until you find them; segmentation is logically prior to (and interacts with) lexical access.

sub_mechanisms.name: lexical_access
sub_mechanisms.definition: Mapping the recovered sound sequence onto stored word forms via competition among candidates that match the input so far (cohort activation, TRACE-style interactive activation), resolving to the best-fitting word.
sub_mechanisms.why: The point of perception is to retrieve words/meaning; the agent's NB-over-clusters recogniser is a (flat) form of this stage.

sub_mechanisms.name: top_down_restoration
sub_mechanisms.definition: Lexical + contextual knowledge fills in missing or masked segments (phonemic restoration): a noise-replaced phoneme is 'heard' if the word/context predicts it.
sub_mechanisms.why: Perception is not purely bottom-up — higher levels feed back, which is why context rescues degraded speech.

sub_mechanisms.name: audiovisual_integration
sub_mechanisms.definition: Visual articulation (lip + jaw movement) is integrated with the acoustic signal; conflicting audio + video can yield a fused percept (the McGurk effect). Perception is inherently multimodal.
sub_mechanisms.why: Shows speech perception targets the underlying ARTICULATORY event, not the acoustics alone — relevant to motor-theoretic accounts.

derivation_rules.name: perception_categorical_signature
then: sharp identification boundary AND poor within-category discrimination
derivation_rules.why: The operational test for categorical perception; distinguishes phonetic from purely psychophysical perception.

derivation_rules.name: perception_inverts_production
then: place + manner + voicing of the consonant
derivation_rules.why: Perception recovers the production triple from the cues coarticulation left in the signal.

derivation_rules.name: perception_needs_normalization
then: speaker_normalization AND context use are required for stable categories
derivation_rules.why: A template-per-phoneme recogniser cannot work; invariance must be RECOVERED, not assumed.

derivation_rules.name: degraded_signal_needs_restoration
if: a lexical + contextual model that PREDICTS the missing part
then: top_down_restoration is required to recover the category the front-end under-resolves
derivation_rules.why: The coarse cochlea + masking leave the bottom-up cue ambiguous or absent; the only remaining information is the redundancy in higher levels, so the segment must be PREDICTED (filled) from the lexical/context model rather than read off the acoustics. Restoration is top-down completion, not a sharper ear.

derivation_rules.name: no_invariant_cue_forces_recovery
if: one phoneme has many spectra and different phonemes can share one spectrum
then: lack_of_invariance means the category must be RECOVERED by top-down + normalization machinery, never matched by a fixed template
derivation_rules.why: There is NO single invariant acoustic pattern per phoneme; a recogniser that assumes a fixed template per phoneme fails. Invariance is therefore not a property of the signal to be measured but a PRECONDITION to be MANUFACTURED — by normalising the talker away, removing coarticulatory context, predicting from the lexicon, and fusing cues. It names WHY all the top-down compensations are needed at once.
